faq: Are hemisphere letters included?
Yes — N/S for latitude, E/W for longitude, derived from the signs. Signed DMS (minus with letters) is a contradiction the output avoids by construction.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 decimals in, DMS of the same point out — format changes, datum never.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
Seconds decimals beyond one are resolution theatre for most sources (0.1″ ≈ 3 m). The converter defaults sensibly; the precision family explains the ladder.
Can I copy the result into GIS software?
GIS prefers decimals — this output is for charts, forms and humans. The Coordinate Converter returns the decimal dress when the software asks.
Seconds exactly 60?
Carried upward properly — the converter normalises 60″ into +1′, and 60′ into +1°, always.
Both coordinates at once?
Yes — the pair converts together, latitudes and longitudes each with their hemisphere.
Zero values?
0°00′00.0″ with the conventional hemisphere — the equator and the prime meridian convert without drama.
Why do forms still want DMS?
Institutional inertia plus genuine chart tradition. The converter exists so the tradition costs you ten seconds, not ten minutes.
Aviation and marine exams?
The conversion these exams test, done here for checking your hand work — learn the steps from the table, then let the tool audit them.
Degrees-minutes instead?
The sibling format (DDM) is produced by the Coordinate Converter — same arithmetic, one subdivision fewer.
My seconds have many decimals.
Display precision — trim with intent using the grain ladder (0.1″ ≈ 3 m is the usual chart choice).
